title: Artemis I Orion’s Moon Flyby – 2022 Mission Overview
description: The uncrewed Orion capsule circles the Moon, reaching record distances for a crewed‑design vehicle. See the journey from launch to Pacific splashdown.

shots.narration: This capsule flew farther from Earth than any spacecraft built for humans.
Here Orion glides past the Moon, a silent sentinel on its 25‑day journey.
Watch the tiny Earth recede as Orion travels toward the far side of the Moon.
This view shows Orion, Earth, and Moon together, a reminder of our home beyond the horizon.
Here Earth sets behind the Moon, captured by cameras on Orion’s solar arrays.
Watch the crescent Earth glow, a fragile blue marble framed by black space.
Orion reached 432,000 km from Earth, the farthest distance any crewed‑design vehicle has traveled.
During re‑entry its heat shield endured about 2,800 °C, protecting the capsule from intense friction.
Now Orion splashes down in the Pacific, completing a 25.5‑day test of future lunar voyages.
Here the Earth and Moon appear side by side, a visual promise of the next crewed Artemis missions.
